topicsPresent: Creation of the Latin Empire after the Fourth Crusade (1204)
Conflict between Tsar Kaloyan and Emperor Baldwin I
Battle of Adrianople (1205) and capture of Baldwin
Latin Empire as a new political power in the Balkans
latin-empire.framingNotes: Original: «По същото време нов съсед на България станала Латинската империя.» / «...българите разгромили „цвета на западното рицарство“ и пленили Балдуин.» Translation: 'At the same time a new neighbor of Bulgaria became the Latin Empire.' / '...the Bulgarians defeated the flower of Western knighthood and captured Baldwin.' The Latin Empire is framed as a foreign crusader state and immediate military opponent of Bulgaria.
latin-empire.analystNotes: Direct 13th-century relevance due to explicit reference to 1204–1205 events. Presented mainly through Bulgarian-Latin conflict.

topicsPresent: Epirus as a successor Byzantine state
Conflict with Bulgaria under Theodore Komnenos
epirus-despotate.framingNotes: Original: «епирският деспот Теодор Комнин... нахлул в българската територия» Translation: 'The despot of Epirus Theodore Komnenos invaded Bulgarian territory.' Epirus is framed as a rival regional power seeking dominance after the fragmentation of Byzantium.
epirus-despotate.analystNotes: Direct 13th-century relevance due to explicit mention of the 1230 campaign and battle. Coverage is event-focused.

topicsPresent: Nicaea as a successor state after 1204
empire-of-nicaea.framingNotes: Original: «...като Епир и Никея... си поставили за цел да възстановят Византия.» Translation: '...such as Epirus and Nicaea set themselves the goal of restoring Byzantium.' Nicaea is framed as one of the key restoration states of Byzantine continuity.
empire-of-nicaea.analystNotes: Direct 13th-century relevance but limited narrative detail. Appears only as part of broader geopolitical context.

topicsPresent: Invasion of Europe under Batu Khan
Destruction in Central and Eastern Europe
mongol-empire.framingNotes: Original: «...Чингис хан, създал гигантска империя... хан Бату... стигнал до Унгария и Полша.» Translation: 'Chinggis Khan created a vast empire... Batu Khan reached Hungary and Poland.' The Mongol Empire is framed as a devastating external force affecting European and Bulgarian development.
mongol-empire.analystNotes: Direct 13th-century relevance with explicit chronological markers and consequences for Bulgaria.

golden-horde.framingNotes: Original: «Българското царство... попаднало под татарска зависимост.» Translation: 'The Bulgarian tsardom fell under Tatar dependence.' The Golden Horde is framed as a dominant external power shaping Bulgarian decline.
golden-horde.analystNotes: Direct 13th-century relevance with sustained impact on internal politics.

holy-roman-empire.framingNotes: Original: «Свещената Римска империя... се превърнала в съюз от стотици почти независими владения.» Translation: 'The Holy Roman Empire became a union of hundreds of almost independent states.' It is framed as a politically fragmented entity in contrast to centralized monarchies.
holy-roman-empire.analystNotes: Indirect 13th-century relevance, presented as long-term structural background.

kingdom-of-hungary.framingNotes: Original: «Унгарското кралство завоювало северозападните земи...» Translation: 'The Kingdom of Hungary conquered the northwestern lands.' Hungary is framed as both a rival and diplomatic partner.
kingdom-of-hungary.analystNotes: Direct relevance due to repeated interaction with Bulgaria in the 13th century.

papal-states.framingNotes: Original: «Папството... оповестило претенциите си за върховна власт...» Translation: 'The Papacy proclaimed its claims to supreme authority.' It is framed as a dominant religious-political force.
papal-states.analystNotes: Indirect relevance as institutional background influencing 13th-century politics.

crusader-states.framingNotes: Original: «Кръстоносците основали в Близкия изток свои държави...» Translation: 'The crusaders founded their own states in the Near East.' These are framed as extensions of Western feudalism abroad.
crusader-states.analystNotes: Direct relevance but only briefly mentioned.
